title: 2011 AMC 12A Problem 10
statement: A pair of standard \(6\)-sided fair dice is rolled once. The sum of the numbers rolled determines the diameter of a circle. What is the probability that the numerical value of the area of the circle is less than the numerical value of the circle’s circumference?

solutions.text:
For diameter \(d,\) area \(\lt\) circumference means \(\dfrac{\pi d^2}{4} \lt \pi d,\) i.e. \(d \lt 4.\) Since \(d \ge 2,\) this needs a sum of \(2\) or \(3.\)

A sum of \(2\) has probability \(\dfrac{1}{36}\) and a sum of \(3\) has probability \(\dfrac{2}{36},\) totaling \(\dfrac{3}{36} = \dfrac{1}{12}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: With diameter \(d,\) the area is \(\dfrac{\pi d^2}{4}\) and the circumference is \(\pi d\)
The inequality \(\dfrac{\pi d^2}{4} \lt \pi d\) reduces to \(d \lt 4\)
